items.title: Anat Cohen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2021
items.q: So many people have preconceptions about the clarinet and they associate it — you know you say jazz and clarinet and people still say, “Ah, Benny Goodman.”

ctx.x: You’ve done very well in the polls, DownBeat, in the last few years, and I wonder if people who are voting for you, if it’s more than the way — how am I — I’m trying to say that people will like what you do not just because of the way you play your instrument, it’s the music you choose to play, at least this is my attitude. Do you think part of your success in those pollings have to do with what you’ve done with combining music and the variety of things you present?

I don’t know. I don’t know, the mystery of the clarinet, and I talked about it at the beginning of our conversation, the certain natural connection. And at the time I remember my first shows as a band leader I played tenor saxophone for the whole show and I played one song on the clarinet, because at the beginning I was, as I mentioned, the clarinet took over my life, right? I was playing saxophone and clarinet was there waiting, lurking, in the corner. So I would play one song on the clarinet in the whole show…
Was there a point — you do some composing and did the clarinet start becoming the instrument you were hearing in your head instead of the saxophone if you were working on a musical idea?
